question: Which of the following Ashokan rock edicts declares prohibition of animal sacrifice?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Major Rock Edict - I**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Major Rock Edict - I** of Emperor Ashoka declares the prohibition of animal sacrifice.
 
• Ashoka, the Mauryan emperor, embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War and promoted non-violence and compassion towards all living beings.
 
• His edicts were inscribed on rocks and pillars throughout his empire to communicate his policies and ethical guidelines.
 
• These edicts reflect Ashoka's dedication to dharma (moral law) and his efforts to create a just and humane society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka** was one of India's greatest emperors, who ruled almost the entire Indian subcontinent from c. 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• His reign is marked by the spread of Buddhism and the establishment of many stupas and viharas (Buddhist monasteries).
 
• The **Major Rock Edicts** are a series of 14 edicts that provide insights into Ashoka's governance, his dedication to Buddhism, and his efforts to promote moral and ethical living.
 
• These edicts are written in various languages including Prakrit, Greek, and Aramaic, reflecting the diverse linguistic landscape of Ashoka's empire.
 
• Ashoka's legacy continues to be celebrated in modern India, where his symbol, the Lion Capital of Ashoka, is used as the national emblem.
